\[
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = \sum_{j=-r}^{r} \sum_{i=-r}^{r} D(i,j)\, I(x+i,\, y+j),
\qquad
D(i,j) = \frac{\left| \mathcal{C}_R \cap \square_{i,j} \right|}{\pi R^2},
\qquad
r = \lceil R - \tfrac{1}{2} \rceil,
\quad
R = 3
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value
- \(R\): Disk radius in pixels
- \(r\): Half-size of the kernel in pixels
- \(\mathcal{C}_R\): The disk of radius R around the center
- \(\square_{i,j}\): The unit square of the kernel cell at offset (i, j)
- \(\lvert \cdot \rvert\): Area

Each weight is the area of the disk of radius R that lies inside that pixel's square, divided by the area of the whole disk. So the weights add up to 1, and pixels on the edge of the disk count only for the part the disk covers. The areas are exact, from the integral of the circle's height.
